notes_list.title: IR Spectroscopy — Functional Group Identification
notes_list.basic_overview: IR spectroscopy probes molecular vibrations and is especially powerful for identifying functional groups through characteristic stretching and bending frequencies.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Carbonyls, O–H, N–H, C≡N and C≡C regions are high-value diagnostic areas. The fingerprint region is highly specific but best used by comparison.
notes_list.examples: A strong C=O absorption near the 1700 cm−1 region is characteristic of many carbonyl compounds; broad O–H bands distinguish alcohols/acids by shape and position.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Sample preparation and physical state matter. Hydrogen bonding broadens O–H/N–H features.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: A vibration is IR-active when it changes molecular dipole moment. Symmetry and coupling affect band intensity and multiplicity.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Frequency depends on bond strength and reduced mass; approximately ν ∝ sqrt(k/μ).
notes_list.common_traps: Do not assign a functional group from one peak without checking neighboring bands and the overall spectrum.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
